questions.text:
The causal continuous-time scalar system dy/dt(t) = a y(t) + u(t) is discretized using the forward Euler method for a zero-order hold input and a uniformly sampled output, with sampling time Ts.

Question 1.1: Determine the values of Ts as a function of a that make the discrete-time system stable. Answers must be justified.

The causal continuous-time scalar system dy/dt(t) = a y(t) + u(t) is discretized using the forward Euler method for a zero-order hold input and a uniformly sampled output, with sampling time Ts.

Question 1.2: Determine for which values of a Euler discretization and exact discretization correspond. Answers must be justified.

Question 2: Consider the discrete-time system y[n] = a y[n-3] + u[n] + 0.5 cos(2 pi n), with a in R. Elaborate on linearity, stability, causality, time-invariance and memorylessness as the parameter a in R varies. Justify your answer.

Consider the cascade of two LTI systems, u[n] -> G_1 -> G_2 -> y[n], with impulse responses h_1[n] = sin(8n) and h_2[n] = a^n s[n], with |a| < 1, where s[n] is the unit step.

Question 3.1: Determine the output of system G_2 if the input is u[n] = delta[n] - a delta[n-1], where delta[n] is the unit impulse. Answers must be justified.

Consider the cascade of two LTI systems, u[n] -> G_1 -> G_2 -> y[n], with impulse responses h_1[n] = sin(8n) and h_2[n] = a^n s[n], with |a| < 1, where s[n] is the unit step.

Question 3.2: Determine the output of the cascade of G_1 and G_2 if the input is u[n] = delta[n] - a delta[n-1]. Answers must be justified.

Consider the signal x[n] = 0 for n <= 0, x[n] = 0 for n odd and n > 0, x[n] = 1/n^2 for n even and n > 0. Let X(Omega) be the Fourier transform of {x[n]}, Y(Omega) = e^(j Omega) X(Omega), Q(Omega) = X(Omega) + Y(Omega), q[n] the inverse Fourier transform of Q(Omega), and r[n] = 0 for n <= 0, r[n] = 0 for n odd and n > 0, r[n] = q[n] - q[n-2] for n even and n > 0.

Question 4: What is r[n]? Answers must be justified.

Let x[n] and y[n] be two periodic signals, both with period N. Let y[n] != 0 for all n, and z[n] = sum_{k=0}^{N-1} x[k] / y[n-k].

Question 5.1: Is the signal z[n] periodic? If yes, what is its period? Answers must be justified.

Let x[n] and y[n] be two periodic signals, both with period N. Let y[n] != 0 for all n, and z[n] = sum_{k=0}^{N-1} x[k] / y[n-k].

Question 5.2: Let X[k], W[k], Z[k] be the Fourier (DFS) coefficients of x[n], w[n] = 1/y[n] and z[n], respectively. Express Z[k] as a function of X[k] and W[k]. Answers must be justified.

Question 6: A signal u has the form u[n] = c_0 + c_1 (-1)^n + c_2 cos(pi/3 n), n = ..., -1, 0, 1, ..., where c_0, c_1, c_2 in R are fixed but unknown constants. Design a causal, stable, LTI filter G so that if u has the form above and y = G u, then y[n] = c_0 for all n. Hint: use cos(pi/3) = 0.5. Answers must be justified.

To identify the coefficients of the transfer function of a causal, stable LTI system of the form H(z) = b_0 / (1 + a_1 z^(-1)), the signal {u[n]} = {(e^(j pi/2 n) + e^(-j pi/2 n)) / 2} is given as input. The Discrete Fourier Series coefficients of the periodic output {y[n]} are {Y[k]} = {0, 3.2 + j1.6, 0, 3.2 - j1.6}. Determine the values of the coefficients a_1 and b_0.

Question 7a: Give the value of a_1. Justify your answer.

To identify the coefficients of the transfer function of a causal, stable LTI system of the form H(z) = b_0 / (1 + a_1 z^(-1)), the signal {u[n]} = {(e^(j pi/2 n) + e^(-j pi/2 n)) / 2} is given as input. The Discrete Fourier Series coefficients of the periodic output {y[n]} are {Y[k]} = {0, 3.2 + j1.6, 0, 3.2 - j1.6}. Determine the values of the coefficients a_1 and b_0.

Question 7b: Give the value of b_0. Justify your answer.

For the following pair of signals {u[n]} and {y[n]}, determine whether {y[n]} can be the output of a discrete-time LTI system given the input {u[n]}. If such a system exists, determine whether it is unique, i.e. fully defined by this input-output relationship. If no such system exists, explain why.

Question 8.1: {u_1[n]} = {e^(jn)}, {y_1[n]} = {2 e^(jn)}. Answers must be justified.

For the following pair of signals {u[n]} and {y[n]}, determine whether {y[n]} can be the output of a discrete-time LTI system given the input {u[n]}. If such a system exists, determine whether it is unique, i.e. fully defined by this input-output relationship. If no such system exists, explain why.

Question 8.2: {u_2[n]} = {cos(n) s[n]}, {y_2[n]} = {2 cos(n) s[n]}, where {s[n]} is the unit step. Answers must be justified.

For the following pair of signals {u[n]} and {y[n]}, determine whether {y[n]} can be the output of a discrete-time LTI system given the input {u[n]}. If such a system exists, determine whether it is unique, i.e. fully defined by this input-output relationship. If no such system exists, explain why.

Question 8.3: {u_3[n]} and {y_3[n]} are both periodic and depicted in the time domain in a figure (n = 0..10, values between 0 and 1) [Figure not included]. Answers must be justified.

For the following pair of signals {u[n]} and {y[n]}, determine whether {y[n]} can be the output of a discrete-time LTI system given the input {u[n]}. If such a system exists, determine whether it is unique, i.e. fully defined by this input-output relationship. If no such system exists, explain why.
